newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tibetans angered by Chinese-Tibetan evening at UN.
newsitem.headline: Tibetans angered by Chinese-Tibetan evening at UN.

text.p: Tibetan organisations exiled in Switzerland protested to the United Nations on Monday over its decision to allow Chinese diplomats to host a Sino-Tibetan cultural evening at the world body's European headquarters in Geneva.
In a petition, they urged Vladimir Petrovsky, U.N. director general in Geneva, to distance himself from what they described as Chinese propaganda abroad to suppress Tibetan culture.
They reminded the U.N. of the 1995 arrest of Tibetan music expert Ngawang Choephel, whom Beijing sentenced to 18 years in prison on espionage charges.
Choephel was arrested while filming a documentary about traditional Tibetan music and dance he feared would be lost because of alleged Chinese efforts to dilute local culture, they said.

"It's ironic that the Chinese authorities present a 'Chinese-Tibetan' performance inside the United Nations but in reality suppress the preservation of Tibetan performing arts in Tibet," said Choechung Wangchuk, member of the Tibetan Youth Congress, which is based in India near the border with Tibet.
A U.N. spokeswoman said the evening was cultural and in line with U.N. rules governing the use of its premises by foreign missions for cultural events.

Tens of thousands of Tibetans, led by their spiritual leader the Dalai Lama, left their homeland after a failed uprising against Chinese rule in 1959. The Dalai Lama won the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize for his non-violent campaign for more autonomy for Tibet.
